descriptionChirho: Repetitive or additive adverb indicating that an action recurs or something is added: 'again,' 'once more,' 'anymore,' 'further,' corresponding to Spanish 'otra vez / más,' Hindi 'फिर,' Arabic 'أَيْضًا,' Korean '다시 / 더,' Swahili 'tena.'

Continuative adverb indicating that a state or condition persists: 'still,' 'yet,' including all inflected forms with pronominal suffixes and interrogative contexts, corresponding to Spanish 'todavía / aún,' Hindi 'अभी,' Arabic 'بَعْدُ / لا يزال,' Korean '아직,' Swahili 'bado.'

Adverb used substantively or adjectivally to denote a different or additional entity: 'another,' 'other,' 'else,' corresponding to Spanish 'otro,' Hindi 'कोई अन्य / कोई और,' Arabic 'غَيْر / آخَر,' Korean '다른,' Swahili 'mwingine.'

Temporal adverb with the preposition בְּ forming a temporal clause meaning 'while still,' 'while yet,' 'as long as [someone] exists,' often with pronominal suffixes indicating the subject of the temporal clause, corresponding to Spanish 'mientras todavía,' Hindi 'जब तक / अभी,' Arabic 'بَينَما / ما دُمتُ,' Korean '아직 ~하는 동안,' Swahili 'wakati bado.'

Adverb denoting unceasing or perpetual duration: 'continually,' 'always,' corresponding to Spanish 'aún' (in perpetual sense), Hindi 'और' (continuous), Arabic 'أَبَدًا' (forever), Korean '여전히,' Swahili 'daima' (always).

Temporal adverb with the preposition מִן indicating origin in time, meaning 'since [one's] existence,' 'from of old,' corresponding to Spanish 'desde siempre,' Hindi 'जन्म से,' Arabic 'مُنْذُ وُجُود,' Korean '살아오는 동안부터,' Swahili 'tangu uzaliwa.'
